claim: Only 310 convictions were recorded from 66,711 women who came through One-Stop Crisis Centres over 23 years, a 0.46 percent conviction rate on that denominator.
notes: Denominator is OCC visitors, not filed cases or disposed cases. Twelve independent measurements range from 0.12 percent to 3.66 percent on different denominators.
sources: One-Stop Crisis Centre programme data, 2001 to July 2024, as published in the live report and methodology

claim: Bangladesh pairs maximum legal severity with near-zero certainty of punishment: death-penalty expansion did not solve reporting attrition, backlog, evidence loss, or witness risk.
notes: Causal claim is supported by the published sequence (severity change, no documented conviction improvement, backlog growth), not by a controlled experiment.
sources: Live report: WCRPA amended October 2020 to add the death penalty; conviction rate did not improve; backlog grew

claim: Critical justice infrastructure remains thin: 14 One-Stop Crisis Centres, two national DNA machines, major unprocessed sample backlogs, and no complete national registry for key case outcomes.
notes: 14 centres are concentrated in divisional headquarters.
sources: Live report investigation metadata; Government submission to the UN Secretary-General, May 2024 (50 of 64 districts with no full OCC)

claim: Forensic DNA backlog is 92%: 1,204 of 1,304 biological samples received in 2025 remained unprocessed at the National Forensic DNA Profiling Laboratory as of September 2025.
sources: MoWCA lab reports and NFDPL data, as published in the live report

claim: The average verdict wait is 2,349 days, over six years, against a statutory 90-day tribunal limit whose compliance rate is unpublished.
notes: 90-day compliance is a confirmed absence, not a measured zero.
sources: 2025 Amendment Ordinance, 90-day limit; compliance rate confirmed absent, gap GA-003

claim: The compound probability of punishment is about 0.0215 percent, or 1 in about 4,650, on the mid-reference model, with a sensitivity range from 0.00034 percent to 0.2756 percent.
notes: Live-report tier is PROBABLE. This is a model, not a direct count, and assumes independence between funnel stages.
sources: Live report methodology, Model A: 0.0146 x 0.59 x 0.025 = 0.0215 percent; Model B 0.0400 percent; Model C 0.2756 percent

claim: 78% of survivors arrive after the 72-hour forensic window (BRAC 2022), while §32 of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act mandates hospital examination — and no institution tracks hospital-refusal compliance.
notes: Aggregate only; no individual case data.
sources: WCRPA section 32; compliance tracking confirmed absent, gap GA-012

claim: In 2024, new WCRPA filings (17,544) outpaced disposals (5,648) by about 3.1 times, adding 11,896 cases to the backlog in one year.
sources: Live report, system failure audit, 2024 filings and disposals
